summary.text: 假 is conventionally analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 亻 relates it to a person, while 叚 supplies a sound cue. A competing account treats 人 as a graphic addition that distinguished the written form in Qin-period use. The evidence does not settle the disagreement or establish which meaning came first.

formation.text: The conventional analysis is phonosemantic: 亻 contributes a person-related meaning and 叚 a phonetic cue. A scholarly alternative proposes that 人 was added to distinguish 假 from 叚 in writing. The dossier does not resolve these accounts or document a detailed graphic sequence.

components.text: 亻 is the conventional side form of 人 and is analyzed here as semantic, contributing a person-related category. The account that it was added to distinguish 假 from 叚 in Qin-period writing remains a proposal.
叚 is conventionally analyzed as the phonetic component. Accounts of its own bronze forms and uses belong to the history of 叚; they do not establish a graphic sequence for 假.

sound.text: In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese notation, 叚 *Cə.kˤraʔ is compared with 假 *Cə.kˤraʔ for the borrow/false entry. The dossier also lists a separate 假 reading *kˤraʔ, so the comparison applies to that listed reading, not every use.

history.text: A scholarly account reports 叚 in excavated pre-Qin texts and 假 in Qin-period documents. It interprets a document dated to 221 BCE as distinguishing lending written with 叚 from borrowing written with 假, and proposes 人 as a differentiating addition. This is a reported interpretation; no manuscript facsimile was inspected for this entry.
Later texts are reported to mix the 叚 and 假 spellings. The dossier does not provide inspected, dated specimens sufficient to trace the graphic changes through later script styles.

Descriptions of 叚 report bronze forms analyzed as 爪, 又, and 石, along with uses read as blessing, fault, interrogative words, and other forms. These descriptions concern 叚 and do not establish an evolutionary path for 假.

uncertainties.text: The conventional analysis treats 亻 as semantic and 叚 as phonetic; a competing proposal treats 人 as a differentiating addition. The dossier does not resolve whether these accounts can be reconciled.
No dated semantic chain from borrowing to falsehood is established. The evidence records both uses, while a proposed path through “simulate” is disputed; their chronology remains unresolved.

The phonetic comparison is reported in one reconstruction system, but the dossier lacks independently verified character-specific pronunciation records and does not establish the historical role by modern readings alone.

senses.text: The Shuowen account glosses 假 as “not true,” and a cited classical example uses it to mean false or not so. The dossier does not securely date the first occurrence.

senses.period: classical text; composition and attestation dating unresolved
senses.text: A cited classical example uses 假 for borrowing a passage. The Qin-period lending-versus-borrowing distinction is a scholarly reading of a dated document, not a directly inspected manuscript in this research.

senses.period: historical and current; first attestation unresolved
senses.text: Dictionary examples record temporary or acting uses, and modern metadata gives “vacation” among current definitions. The evidence does not establish when these uses arose or how they relate to borrowing or falsehood.

limitations.text: The cited senses do not establish a relative chronology or continuous semantic development. In particular, the proposed path from borrowing through simulation to falsehood remains disputed.

overview.text: 假 conventionally combines a person-related element with 叚 as a sound cue. It is used for “false” and “borrow,” but the evidence does not establish which use came first.

components.text: 亻 is the side form of 人 and supplies the conventional person-related meaning; its proposed role as a differentiating addition is debated.
叚 is conventionally treated as the sound component; the historical comparison supports one reading, not every use of 假.

relationships.text: In the conventional analysis of 假, 亻 contributes a person-related meaning; a competing account treats 人 as a differentiating addition.
The conventional analysis assigns 叚 the sound role, and one Old Chinese reconstruction lists matching forms for 叚 and 假. The evidence does not make this comparison apply to every reading.
